newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends on six-week low in tech selloff.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends on six-week low in tech selloff.

text.p: COMEX copper spiralled to a six-week low Tuesday, dragged down by a selloff which began on LME amid indications of an approaching traditional seasonal slowdown in the key U.S. market, dealers said.
The selling was largely technical once LME three months broke below the key $2,400 a tonne level. No major fresh fundamental developments prompted the move, dealers said.

Resumption of talks at Inco Ltd's striking Sudbury operations Wednesday and reopening of the weather-hit El Teniente mine in Chile were largely coincidental rather than a cause of the selloff, dealers said.
"There were no buyers out there and just selling into vacuum," John Tyree of FIMAT Futures said. "We started to break technical levels and everyone headed for the exit at the same time."

COMEX July copper settled 6.05 cents weaker at 112.15 cents a lb, traded 118.00 to 111.60 cents. Spot June went out 5.90 cents off at 112.70 cents, while September, soon to become most active, ended 5.45 cents lower at 110.75 cents.
Volume was heavy at an estimated 20,000 lots.
The selloff was coupled with an easing in the LME cash to three months backwardation to $110/$120, down from $135/$140 when COMEX opened.
"The fundamental picture is the same as it was a week ago when we were at 123 cents a lb," William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.
The warning signs of a pause in the upward trend were clear, he added.

The CFTC Commitment of Traders report on COMEX copper showing speculators overwhelmingly long told the market to be careful, O'Neill said. Prices were headed lower short-term before resuming an upward climb.

In the U.S. physical market dealers expected the traditional summer slowdown to make itself felt soon. The tightness in cathode supplies had eased and the spike in nearby premiums in the Northeastern region was over, traders said.
At close of trade Monday, open interest in the July COMEX contract was still high at 20,166 lots with only a few days before first notice day Friday.
By close Tuesday, cash LME was the equivalent of 115.98 cents, a whopping 3.28 cents above spot COMEX. Traders expected metal to move from COMEX to LME warehouses in the U.S.
